title: Avoiding Reverse Falls in Drainage Piping
description: One of the most common and damaging mistakes in drainage installation is failing to maintain consistent downward slope, leading to 'reverse falls.' When a pipe sags or is installed level, wastewater loses its carrying velocity. Solid waste settles at the low point, while liquids bypass it, resulting in progressive pipe blockages and frequent backups. Professional installation requires continuous support, proper hanger spacing, and careful verification using a level to ensure gravity does correct work throughout the entire run. Learning to identify and prevent reverse falls saves plumbers and property owners from costly tear-outs and chronic drainage failures.
